data-mindset-story.text: The Superpower. AJ, Nia, and Malik are walking the feed like detectives. The superpower is not magic. It's the ability to see data everywhere. Right now, they're surrounded by information. Every post, every review, every comment is data waiting to be discovered.

Social Media as Phone Book. Nia compares social media to a phone book of data. It's not just people posting selfies. It's millions of people telling you what they think, what they want, and what problems they have. Malik likes that the raw material is already out there.

Data Sources Everywhere. AJ and Malik keep listing the sources: social media shows opinions and trends. Reviews reveal what people love and hate. Comments show real reactions. Local listings, news, public stats. Data is literally everywhere once you learn to see it.

Data Becomes Insight. Nia makes the point clean: data, when you know how to collect and analyze it, becomes insight. Insight is understanding. Understanding leads to solutions. That is how problem solvers operate.

algorithms-story.text: Two Algorithms. AJ sets the frame: there are two algorithms you need to understand because they control most of how you find and receive information. One puts you in control. The other puts the platform in control. Nia is already side-eyeing the second one.

Search Algorithm. Search means you have a goal and you go find it. When AJ searches Google or YouTube, he decides what he wants and the algorithm tries to match it. Malik loves that better search terms mean better results. This is a skill.

Recommendation Algorithm. Recommendation means the platform decides what you see. Nia watches the feeds that keep people hooked. TikTok, YouTube homepage, Instagram Explore - they watch what you engage with and show you more of the same.

The Critical Difference. AJ makes the difference obvious: search means you're in control and you choose what to find. Recommendation means the algorithm chooses what you see. Problem solvers use search more than recommendation. They know what they're looking for and go get it.

Be Intentional. Malik keeps it practical: don't let algorithms choose your information for you. Be intentional about what you engage with. When you need to learn something, search for it. Don't wait for it to be recommended.

analysis-story.text: Collection is Simple. Malik says data collection isn't complicated. It is just being intentional about gathering information instead of passively scrolling past it. You see data every day. You just need to capture it.

The Collection Pattern. AJ gives the pattern: define what you want to know, identify where the data lives, collect it systematically, then look for patterns. Nia says it is simple when you line it up like that.

Look for Patterns. Raw data is just numbers and words. Malik spots the first pattern in the noise. Insights come from patterns. If ten reviews mention slow service, that's a pattern. If everyone praises the vibe, that's a pattern.
Ask Why. Once you see patterns, AJ asks why. Why do people complain about this? Why do they love that? Go deeper than the surface. Use your six levels deep skills to understand root causes.

Find the Gaps. Nia wants to know what is missing. What are people asking for that does not exist? Gaps equal opportunities. Every unmet need is a potential solution waiting to be built. Data reveals where to focus.

Draw Conclusions. AJ closes the loop: based on the patterns, what can you conclude? What would you recommend? This is where data becomes useful, when it informs action. Nia calls it the difference between analysis and noise.
